title: LLM inference serving, Part 6: quantization and speculative decoding
tldr: Why decode's memory-bound step leaves two levers: read fewer bytes per token or get more tokens per read. Bytes per parameter for BF16, FP8, INT8 and INT4, weight-only versus weight-and-activation schemes, GPTQ and AWQ at the mechanism level, what vLLM v0.31.0 runs on Ampere and Hopper and NVIDIA's FP8 figures halved to dense, an FP8 KV cache doubling Part 2's capacity, how quality loss is measured and what GPTQ and Hugging Face report, speculative decoding's draft-and-verify round with rejection sampling that keeps the output distribution, expected tokens per pass and vLLM's acceptance metrics, the ngram, draft_model, EAGLE and MTP proposers, why weight-only formats and speculation lose their edge at high batch, the ITL versus TPOT trap, Snowflake compression and optimistic-locking analogies and where they break, a step-through round, a calculator, a tested estimator and an interview drill.
